correctness.rationale: The upper bound is forced by zero/one counts and cyclic-transition monotonicity. All length-2 through length-14 binary necklaces are exhaustively generated and two independent exact subsequence tests agree on exactly one failing rotation orbit, the word 00000101111101. A table of 14 length-six necklace embeddings establishes its lower bound. A separate cyclic-run argument proves 0010011 is impossible for the complete family 0^a 1 0 1^b 0 1, for all integers a,b>=1; containment of the a=b=5 member proves the universal length-six lower bound for a,b>=5. The standalone package checker ran successfully on the actual package source bytes.

value.rationale: The first failure of the obvious capacity bound for a natural adaptive circular subsequence channel is a sharp, structurally motivated boundary, not an arbitrary short numerical statistic. The result supplies a complete first-exception classification plus an infinite family with a word-equation-style obstruction. It distinguishes the order of existential and universal cut quantifiers, which is important for determining whether different requested subsequences may select different starting cuts.
